column1: # Reviewed allowlist of ProVerif resolution heuristics, precision settings and output settings. The transcript-fidelity test scans every .pv and .pvl file under proofs/pro-verif, including generated files, after removing comments as ProVerif does (nested, each comment a token separator). It fails on any axiom, restriction, elimtrue or clauses declaration, and it requires every set, param, nounif, select, noselect, lemma and secrecy-assumption (not) declaration and every [precise] input to match exactly one entry below, with no stale entries. It also scans every string literal of every Python file under proofs/pro-verif, because the checkers and generators write ProVerif text at run time: a keyword counts there when it starts a literal or follows a format placeholder, a period, a brace or a comment end; forbidden declarations fail, and every other declaration except secrecy assumptions, which ProVerif verifies itself, and every [precise] needs an entry under the Python file's path.

# Columns, separated by one tab: path, kind, occurrence count in that file, declaration with whitespace collapsed (or [precise]), and the documentation paragraph that explains why the entry does not change what a verdict means.
